references.text: Joseph gave orders to put the money back in his brothers' sacks – this is the direct cause of what they discover in verse 35.

One of the brothers already discovered his money in his sack on the way home, which created fear. In verse 35, all the brothers find their money, and the fear spreads to the whole group and their father.
Jacob's immediate reaction upon discovering the money: he complains that he is losing his sons, showing the deep fear described in v.35.
The brothers tell Joseph's steward about when they discovered the money in their sacks, and he reassures them – a direct reference back to the event in 42:35.
Joseph orders that his silver cup be placed in Benjamin's sack, parallel to how the brothers' money was returned in their sacks, creating again anxiety and fear.
The brothers refer to the earlier incident where the money was found in their sacks as proof of their honesty regarding the silver cup.
Direct narrative connection: 42:27 is the first discovery that leads to the collective fear in 42:35.
Narrative connection: 44:11 is the second major discovery in the sack that completes the test the brothers were subjected to.
Clear theological contrast: Money triggers fear and accusation in Genesis, while it triggers joy and betrayal in Matthew.
Clear theological contrast: Money triggers fear among the brothers (conscience) versus joy among the priests (betrayal).
